statement: Submission deadline stated as "29 October 2026 at 14:00" with no time zone. The portal at ITB-9.9 is a .gov service operating in UTC; the Site is US Gulf Coast (CDT, UTC−5). A bid submitted at 14:00 local is 19:00 UTC — five hours late.
expected_action: Flag; draft clarification question; add to submission checklist as an unresolved item blocking submission

statement: Technical scoring awards zero points for "shall" compliance. Only "will" (2 pts) and "may" (1 pt) score. A bid fully compliant with every mandatory requirement and nothing else scores 0 of 40 technical. Either the scoring is inverted or the intent is undisclosed.
expected_action: Flag as a scoring ambiguity with material bid-strategy impact; clarification question; feed to the bid-score optimiser as an unresolved parameter

statement: Published budget $15,000,000. Fully compliant bid computes to ~$15.9M — 6% over.
expected_action: Surface at first costing; drive the alternative-proposal path; feed the § 01 scoring model

requires: company facts (bonding line, CVs, past projects)
statement: Surety bonding capacity of $20,000,000 required for a single project. Kestrel's current single-project line is $18,000,000.
expected_action: Flag as a solvable constraint on Day 1; options: increase line (~3 weeks, cost), co-surety, or JV under ITB-3.10

requires: company facts (bonding line, CVs, past projects)
statement: Site visit attendance mandatory; every attendee must hold a valid TWIC; no escorted access provided. A bidder without TWIC-holding staff is eliminated before it can bid. Three obligations in two clauses.
expected_action: Split into atomic requirements; check Kestrel TWIC holders against the 24 Sep date; flag lead time for a new TWIC (~2–3 weeks) against a 10-day window

statement: An alternative requires a fully compliant offer to be submitted as well, separately priced. Doubles the estimating and technical writing effort.
expected_action: Flag to bid manager as a resourcing impact; feed both cases to the P&L workbench

statement: 50 MB per-file limit; the portal rejects a larger file without notification to the Bidder. A technical package with drawings and datasheets routinely exceeds this.
expected_action: Add to submission checklist as a hard constraint; flag the silent-failure risk

statement: Four hard copies, sealed, marked, with Package B in a separately sealed inner envelope, delivered by the same deadline as the portal upload. Physical delivery to a Gulf Coast address with no stated grace.
expected_action: Split; add to submission checklist with a lead-time backstop

statement: No pricing of any kind in Package A or C; disclosure causes rejection. Datasheets and CVs frequently carry list prices or day rates.
expected_action: Flag as a document-scrubbing obligation before submission

statement: 100% performance bond + 100% payment bond + 10% maintenance bond valid 36 months from Final Acceptance. The maintenance bond duration is the outlier.
expected_action: Price the financing cost; flag the 36-month maintenance bond against Kestrel's standard

statement: "Bidders shall not qualify a Yes." Many real requirements are compliant only with a stated interpretation. Forces either a bare Yes that overstates, or a No that loses points.
expected_action: Flag; the correct route is a clarification question under ITB-6.5, not a qualified Yes

statement: A Bidder who does not raise an ambiguity by the question deadline is deemed to have priced the requirement as written. This converts every unraised defect into a priced obligation.
expected_action: This clause is why clarification questions are a deadline-bound deliverable, not a note. Feed every UNVERIFIABLE, IMPOSSIBLE and ENG-CONFLICT finding into the Q&A list before 05 Oct

statement: Site visit 24 Sep; question deadline 05 Oct. Eleven days to digest a mandatory site visit and produce questions across a 13-document package.
expected_action: Flag as a programme risk on the bid itself; candidate for an extension request under ITB-6.6

statement: Section 889 stated explicitly, including "as a component or original equipment manufacturer supply to another brand". Activates the catalogue trap: one vendor is an OEM rebrand of a covered entity.
expected_action: Every proposed product must be checked for covered-entity origin, not just brand name. Hard rejection regardless of technical or commercial merit

statement: Order of precedence places the General Conditions above the Technical Specification. A commercial term therefore overrides a technical one where they conflict.
expected_action: Not a defect in itself, but a rule the conflict-resolution logic must apply when reconciling CONFLICT findings

statement: Obligation to destroy all SSI and certify destruction within 30 days if unsuccessful — buried in a confidentiality clause, not a numbered deliverable.
expected_action: Recover as a requirement; it is a post-bid obligation with a deadline and a cost

statement: Weekly certified payrolls under Davis-Bacon — a recurring administrative cost over a 22–32 month programme, stated in a federal-provisions clause rather than in the Scope of Work.
expected_action: Recover; price the administrative burden

statement: Build America Buy America domestic content on iron and steel, manufactured products and construction materials. Fence posts, cabinets, poles and conduit are all caught.
expected_action: Recover; check every catalogue item for domestic content; a further filter on top of Section 889

statement: Scope summarised as a single sentence containing nine distinct system scopes.
expected_action: Split into nine; each becomes a section of the technical response

statement: Contact with any Authority officer other than the Procurement Officer "may result in disqualification" — including, read literally, the operational staff a bidder must speak to during the mandatory site visit.
expected_action: Flag as a low-severity operational contradiction; note for the site visit team

statement: PDR approval at day 60 is a precondition to placing any procurement order. Long-lead items (crash gates, thermal, radar, turnstiles) run 20–40 weeks. First delivery M5 is due day 210. Day 60 + approval + 280 days lead = day ~350 at best. The milestone table cannot be achieved as written.
expected_action: Prove by arithmetic; clarification question before 05 Oct; if unresolved it is a priced delay risk under ITB-6.5

statement: SAT (M9) due day 510 and includes a 30-day continuous soak. Final Acceptance (M11) due day 540 but requires 90 consecutive days without a Severity 1 or 2 fault. 510 + 90 = day 600. The milestone table is internally impossible by 60 days.
expected_action: Arithmetic proof; this is the cleanest provable internal conflict in the package

requires: company facts (bonding line, CVs, past projects)

expected_action: Solvable constraint. Options: alternative PM · marine-experienced deputy · raise in Q&A before 05 Oct

statement: $25,000 liquidated damages per occurrence for substitution — and for a named person not in fact performing the role from mobilisation. Directly punishes bidding aspirational CVs.
expected_action: Flag to legal and to resourcing; forces a genuine availability check on all six Key Personnel

statement: Contractor provides all escorts; cost never mentioned; GCC-3.4 deems it included and GCC-3.5 bars any claim. Every non-TWIC trades worker needs a TWIC escort at FSP ratios, often 1:5.
expected_action: Recover as a requirement; price it explicitly; flag the risk transfer

statement: 18 months / 540 days against 22–32 months realistic on a live terminal.
expected_action: Flag; feed the schedule-credibility component of the technical score

statement: Training delivery, training materials and course recording all use "will", which under ITB-2.1 makes them optional. Plainly intended as mandatory. Three instances in one section.
expected_action: Detect the modality inconsistency against the stated convention; clarification question

statement: "Training shall be of a standard satisfactory to the Authority." No criterion.
expected_action: Clarification question proposing an objective acceptance criterion

statement: The Authority "will review and respond to design submissions" — no period stated. The Contractor must respond to any Authority query within 5 working days. Asymmetric, and it sits on the critical path through PDR and CDR.
expected_action: Flag the asymmetry; clarification question requesting an Authority response time

statement: "whether or not each item is expressly enumerated" and "shall be deemed included". Open-ended scope with no boundary.
expected_action: Flag; the BOQ becomes indicative rather than definitive, which changes how the estimate must be built

statement: Supply is in batches tied to Authority-issued sector releases, issued "as terminal operations permit", with GCC-4.4 disclaiming any obligation to act in any period — while the Contractor carries the 18-month programme.
expected_action: Flag as an uncontrollable programme dependency; clarification question seeking a release commitment

statement: A single sentence containing twelve distinct design deliverables.
expected_action: Split into twelve atomic requirements

statement: Ten systems enumerated as one scope requirement.
expected_action: Split into ten

statement: Continuous manned guarding of every open perimeter sector until the new detection line is operational, at Contractor cost. Across 8 sectors over 5–8 months.
expected_action: Recover; price the guarding

statement: The Authority's own costs of witnessing a repeated test are borne by the Contractor. Uncapped.
expected_action: Flag; price a contingency

statement: All remaining Site spares handed to the Authority at warranty expiry at no cost.
expected_action: Recover; price the spares as consumed

statement: Full configuration backup at Final Acceptance and at each warranty anniversary — a recurring obligation buried in a documentation clause.
expected_action: Recover; price three additional visits

statement: Project Manager on Site not fewer than three days per week for 18 months; Site Safety Officer full-time; Commissioning Engineer full-time through two phases.
expected_action: Recover the presence obligations; they are a large labour cost stated as a qualification

statement: Site hours 07:00–17:00 Mon–Fri, with out-of-hours work requiring approval "not unreasonably withheld". The phasing at SOW-8 and the M8 cutover require night and weekend work. Permission is necessary but not guaranteed.
expected_action: Flag; clarification question seeking pre-agreed out-of-hours windows

statement: Liquidated damages at 0.5% of Contract Price per week, with NO CAP, accruing until Final Acceptance. On $15.4M that is $77,000/week indefinitely. Kestrel standard is 0.3%/week capped at 10%.
expected_action: NO-BID TRIGGER — must fire within minutes of intake, from the contract document alone

statement: "The liability of the Contractor under this Contract shall be unlimited."
expected_action: NO-BID TRIGGER

statement: Consequential, indirect and special losses expressly included, and expressly extended to civil penalties imposed on the Authority under 33 CFR 101, 33 CFR 105 and 49 CFR 1520. Regulatory fines on a third party are not insurable in the ordinary market.
expected_action: NO-BID TRIGGER — and the uninsurability point is the argument that wins the negotiation
demo_note: No-bid trigger — consequential loss including regulatory fines

statement: 15% of the Contract Price — ~$2.3M — payable only on pre-gate cutover "during a vessel-free window nominated by the Authority". The trigger is entirely outside the Contractor's control.
expected_action: Model the cash curve with the milestone deferred; quantify the working capital cost

statement: 10% retention on every payment, released only at the expiry of the 36-month warranty. On $15.4M that is $1.54M held for approximately 4.5 years.
expected_action: Quantify the financing cost; it is a material and frequently mispriced line

statement: 45-day payment terms, and the whole invoice may be held where any part is disputed.
expected_action: Model; flag the single-line-dispute exposure

statement: The Contractor must proceed with a Variation before its value is agreed.
expected_action: Flag; combine with GCC-8.4's 10% OH&P cap

statement: Overhead and profit on Variations capped at 10% in aggregate — below Kestrel's blended margin, so every Variation is dilutive.
expected_action: Flag to finance; feed the margin model

statement: No-damage-for-delay, expressly extending to delay caused by the Authority's own act, omission, default or breach. Sole remedy is an extension of time.

statement: Contractor's claims time-barred at 10 days with a full programme impact analysis required; the Authority is under no obligation to act within any period at all.

expected_action: Flag; this is the "penalties beyond LDs" red flag

statement: Where a manufacturer withdraws support during the 36-month warranty, the Contractor replaces the item at its own cost. Across ~174 cameras and a full software estate this is an open-ended obligation.

statement: Termination for convenience with no loss of profit on the unexecuted portion and no other loss or expense.
expected_action: Flag

statement: Shortage of materials, supplier failure and permit delay expressly excluded from Force Majeure — on a project with 20–40 week long leads and a certification pathway.
expected_action: Flag

statement: Bonds must be increased on any Variation within 14 days at the Contractor's cost.
expected_action: Price

statement: Disputes determined by the Authority's own Executive Director, final and binding unless proceedings are commenced within 90 days. The Authority judges its own case.
expected_action: Flag to legal

statement: The Contractor is required to prepare and submit the Cybersecurity Plan required by 33 CFR 101.630 to the Coast Guard for approval. That obligation falls on the owner or operator of the facility, not on a contractor. A contractor cannot submit a facility cybersecurity plan for a facility it does not operate, and the Coast Guard would not accept it.
expected_action: Regulatory conflation. Clarification question proposing the correct split: the Contractor supplies the technical content and evidence; the Authority remains the submitting party

statement: FAR clauses incorporated by reference as though the FAR applied directly. A port authority spending FEMA grant money is not a federal agency; the operative regime is 2 CFR Part 200 Subpart D, which imports the underlying statutes. Reciting FAR clause numbers without the 2 CFR hook is a drafting error with real consequences for interpretation.
expected_action: Flag; note that the substantive obligations mostly survive via 2 CFR 200 Appendix II, but the mechanism is wrong

statement: Insurance maintained for six years after the Contract, including Cyber Liability at $5M and Maritime Employers' Liability at $5M. A long-tail cost stated as a condition.
expected_action: Recover; price the run-off

statement: Source code escrow for any bespoke software, Authority as beneficiary.
expected_action: Recover; price the escrow agent

statement: Indemnity applies irrespective of the Authority's own negligence, save only where the Authority is solely negligent.
expected_action: Flag to legal and to insurers — insurability is doubtful

statement: Pixel density ≥ 80 px/m at the far edge of the detection zone. Not a datasheet field. Must be computed from sensor width, horizontal resolution, lens focal length and design range: px/m = H_res / (2 · d · tan(½·HFoV)). Three catalogue cameras satisfy every stated numeric requirement and fail this one.
expected_action: The flagship constraint. Parse to a computed constraint; evaluate per camera position; flag failures with the computed value, not a pass/fail

statement: −40 °C operation and IEEE 802.3af PoE at ≤ 15.4 W. A camera heater rated to −40 °C draws 25–60 W. The two requirements cannot both be satisfied by any product.
expected_action: Detect across two adjacent requirements; clarification question proposing 802.3at/bt or a relaxed lower limit

statement: WDR ≥ 140 dB. The catalogue's best perimeter camera is exactly 140 dB. Compliant with zero margin — one datasheet revision from non-compliance.
expected_action: Compliant, but flagged as zero-margin technical risk in the matrix

statement: IP67 and IK10. Candidates at IP66 fail; a candidate at IP68 passes with margin. Ordinal scale, not string equality.
expected_action: Ordinal comparison, not exact match

statement: PTZ cameras required at IP66 minimum, while fixed cameras at the same locations require IP67. Internally inconsistent environmental policy on one perimeter.
expected_action: Flag the inconsistency; clarification question

statement: ASTM F2656 rating M50 / P1. A two-part ordinal. A gate rated M50 / P2 satisfies the vehicle-and-speed axis and fails the penetration axis. Subtle, realistic, and invisible to string matching.
expected_action: Decompose into two ordinal constraints and evaluate independently

statement: Crash-rated sliding gate full cycle in ≤ 10 seconds at a 24 ft clear opening. Commercial crash gates operate at 27–48 ft/min, giving a 24 ft gate a 30–55 second cycle. No compliant product exists.
expected_action: Flag as unachievable; clarification question proposing barrier arms for throughput with the crash gate for lock-down — which is the correct engineering answer anyway

statement: Transaction ≤ 20 seconds, and ≥ 180 vehicles per lane per hour. 3600 ÷ 180 = exactly 20 s, leaving zero time for vehicle movement between transactions.
expected_action: Arithmetic proof; the lane cannot achieve the stated throughput

statement: The 20-second transaction contains a TOS query (≤2 s), a watchlist query (≤3 s), OCR, credential and RFID reads — and an operator decision at the C&C station, which is unbounded. Not achievable with a human in the loop.
expected_action: Cross-document detection; clarification question

refs: TS-A.1 to A.3, A.10 to A.12
ref_raw: TS-A.1 to A.3, A.10 to A.12
statement: Taut-wire detection fence, 20 wires, 10 ft post spacing, full 8,200 lf, with a 12 ft patrol road — while TS-B.27 already requires AI video analytics at Pd ≥ 95%. A redundant second detection layer at ~$1,059,000 of price, which also raises the nuisance alarm rate in a coastal wind environment.
expected_action: The headline alternative proposal. Generate the technical justification: equal Pd, lower NAR, $1.06M saved
demo_note: Taut-wire fence is redundant — $1.06 M alternative

statement: TWIC readers required to be on the QTL and to perform biometric fingerprint verification "in accordance with the TWIC Reader Rule". The Reader Rule applies to Risk Group A facilities — bulk dangerous cargo — and not to container terminals, where 33 CFR 105.255 requires visual inspection. Over-specified against the legal baseline.
expected_action: Flag the regime error; alternative proposal offering contactless CHUID/FASC-N with Canceled Card List check, ~$95,000 saved

statement: FICAM Approved Products List and FIPS 201-3 compliance required. FICAM and PIV apply to federal agency facilities. A port authority marine terminal is not one; its credential is TWIC, not PIV.
expected_action: Flag; clarification question distinguishing the TWIC regime from the federal PIV regime

statement: UL 294 8th Edition, Level IV on all four axes — destructive attack, line security, endurance and standby power simultaneously. A rare and costly combination; typical listings pair Level I line security with Level IV endurance.
expected_action: Alternative proposal candidate; flag the cost driver

statement: Fully redundant fibre ring serving every field cabinet, including low-criticality yard positions.
expected_action: Alternative: ring on the security backbone, spur to low-criticality. ~$120,000

statement: Continuous recording at full frame rate and full resolution on all 174 cameras for 30 days.
expected_action: Alternative: rate-shaping on low-activity yard cameras after day 7. ~$140,000

statement: "adequate video quality for the identification of individuals" — no DORI class, no pixel density.
expected_action: Clarification question proposing DORI Identify at 250 px/m

statement: "Lighting shall be sufficient to support the performance required." Unbounded, and it is the Contractor who carries the risk.
expected_action: Clarification question proposing a lux level at a stated plane

statement: "shall not be defeated by wind, rain, hail, wildlife or debris common to the Site" — an absolute, untestable obligation.
expected_action: Clarification question; propose NAR as the measurable proxy

statement: "lighting appropriate to continuous screen-based work" — no lux value, no plane, no uniformity.
expected_action: Clarification question proposing 300–500 lux at desk level

statement: Classification accuracy ≥ 95% with no test method, no dataset, no environmental conditions and no per-class breakdown. Accuracy at night in rain is a different number from accuracy at noon.
expected_action: Clarification question proposing a test protocol and per-class, per-condition reporting

statement: Pd ≥ 95% against four defeat methods with no trial count and no confidence level. 19 of 20 trials is 95% and proves very little.
expected_action: Clarification question proposing trials and a confidence interval

statement: MTBF ≥ 60,000 hours with no confidence interval and no definition of failure.
expected_action: Clarification question

statement: "will provide a means of recording operator actions" and "Thermal cameras will be integrated with the surface radar" — optional under ITB-2.1, plainly intended as mandatory. Two further instances.

statement: Eight sequential obligations in one requirement — plate, chassis, RFID, credential, Canceled Card List, TOS query, watchlist query, operator decision.
expected_action: Split into eight

statement: No equipment "scheduled for end of production or end of support within five (5) years of Final Acceptance" — a procurement filter stated as a general requirement. Eliminates catalogue items on lifecycle grounds alone.
expected_action: Recover; apply as a catalogue filter alongside Section 889 and BABA

statement: Declaration of manufacturing origin of the device and of its image sensor, video encoder and network interface. This is the clause that makes the Section 889 OEM-rebrand trap operative in practice.

statement: A field-of-view calculation for every camera position — a design deliverable stated in the video section rather than in SOW-7. 174 calculations.

statement: Video retention 30 days. Annex A states 45 days. Cross-document contradiction.

statement: Query the National Crime Information Center for every driver and every vehicle at the pre-gate. NCIC access is restricted to authorised criminal justice agencies. A port authority is not one, and a systems integrator cannot deliver this at any price.
expected_action: The flagship impossibility. Not expensive, not ambiguous — unlawful as specified. Clarification question proposing the lawful alternative: TWIC Canceled Card List, TSA vetting status, ALPR hotlist through a law enforcement partner, and a locally administered deny list

statement: Watchlist interface unavailable → fail closed, no vehicle admitted until restored. Read literally, an API outage stops every truck entering the port.

statement: "shall not require any modification to the Terminal Operating System", while IF-2.3 demands a synchronous booking query most TOS installations do not expose without configuration or an interface module.

statement: Watchlist results retained 12 months, with no stated legal basis, no consent mechanism and no treatment of driver biometric data.

statement: The specified lens cannot meet the specified pixel density. TS-B.13 requires a varifocal lens of 2.8–12 mm. TS-B.25 requires ≥ 80 px/m at the far edge of the detection zone, and the zone extents on SEC-201/202 give a 55 m design range. At the longest available focal length: HFoV = 2·arctan(5.6 / 24) = 26.27°; coverage at 55 m = 25.67 m; 1920 ÷ 25.67 = 74.8 px/m. Below the requirement. The tender specifies a lens range whose best case fails its own performance requirement.
expected_action: The strongest computed defect in the package. Requires combining a lens spec, a sensor spec, a performance requirement and a drawing. Resolution is either a 14 mm minimum focal length or a 50 m spacing (≈ 5 more cameras) — both priced
demo_note: Specified lens cannot meet the specified pixel density

statement: OSDP Secure Channel and Wiegand in the same breath. TS-C.26 requires OSDP v2.2 with Secure Channel and "Wiegand shall be provided as a parallel output for compatibility with the existing system". Wiegand is unencrypted and unsupervised, which defeats both the OSDP Secure Channel requirement and UL 294 Level IV line security at TS-D.2. Annex A-5.3 further states the existing access control system is being replaced, so there is nothing to be compatible with.
expected_action: Detect across three documents; clarification question proposing OSDP only

statement: Minimum illumination stated as 0.005 lux colour / 0.0005 lux monochrome at F1.4, 1/30 s, 30 IRE. Manufacturers publish at 30 IRE or 50 IRE, with AGC and frame-integration on or off, and the figures differ by an order of magnitude. The convention is stated but the AGC and sens-up conditions are not.
